new: כאשר רופא מומחה במוסד קבע שמטופל בגיר אינו מסוגל להבין בענייניו הרפואיים ונזקק לטיפול שיש דחיפות לתיתו (ושאינו אשפוז פסיכיאטרי) (§14א(א)), ואין לו מיופה כוח או אפוטרופוס לענייניו הרפואיים — עובד סוציאלי במוסד הרפואי, באישור מנהל המוסד (בקופת חולים — הרופא המחוזי), רשאי לתת לאדם בגיר אישור בכתב לשמש "מקבל החלטות זמני", לפי סדר הקדימויות שבסעיף 14ב ובכפוף לחריג שבסעיף 14ב(ה) למי ששמו נקוב בייפוי כוח שטרם נכנס לתוקף או בהנחיות מקדימות, בתנאי שיפעל לטובת המטופל, נתן הסכמה והצהרה בכתב והמטופל לא הביע התנגדות לאישורו (§14א(ב)(4)–(6)).

old: מקבל החלטות זמני (§14א): כאשר רופא מומחה קבע שמטופל בגיר אינו מסוגל להבין בענייניו הרפואיים וזקוק לטיפול דחוף (לא אשפוז פסיכיאטרי), ואין לו מיופה כוח/אפוטרופוס רפואי — עובד סוציאלי במוסד, באישור מנהל המוסד, יכול לאשר בן משפחה כמקבל החלטות זמני, לתוקף 6 חודשים מיום שניתן.
new: מקבל החלטות זמני (§14א): כאשר רופא מומחה קבע שמטופל בגיר אינו מסוגל להבין בענייניו הרפואיים וזקוק לטיפול דחוף (לא אשפוז פסיכיאטרי), ואין לו מיופה כוח/אפוטרופוס רפואי — עובד סוציאלי במוסד, באישור מנהל המוסד, יכול לאשר אדם בגיר כמקבל החלטות זמני לפי סדר הקדימויות בסעיף 14ב ובכפוף לחריג בסעיף 14ב(ה) למי ששמו נקוב בייפוי כוח שטרם נכנס לתוקף או בהנחיות מקדימות, בתנאי שיפעל לטובת המטופל, נתן הסכמה והצהרה בכתב והמטופל לא הביע התנגדות לאישורו (§14א(ב)(4)–(6)), לתוקף 6 חודשים מיום שניתן.

old: Environmental: extrinsic factors contribute to 35–45% of injurious falls; 1/4 to 1/2 of falls occur away from home; a stairs fall carries ~2x the injury risk of other falls (p636–637).
new: Environmental: it has been estimated that extrinsic factors are involved in 35–45% of injurious falls; 1/4 to 1/2 of falls occur away from home; a stairs fall carries ~2x the injury risk of other falls (p636–637).

old: TUG test: rise from chair, walk 3 meters, turn, return, sit; a 25-study systematic review found limited predictive value and no validated cut-point (p637).
new: TUG test: rise from chair, walk 3 meters, turn, return, sit; a 25-study systematic review found limited predictive value in community-dwelling older adults and no cut-point for impaired performance could be recommended (p637).

old: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; keep post-op spectacle power change < ±0.75 diopter (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).
new: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; one prospective cohort study associated cataract surgery with fewer falls provided post-op spectacle lens power updates were cautious (less than ±0.75 diopter change) (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).

old: CSA is two to three times more prevalent at age 65–90 vs 39–64; upwards of 50% of stable heart-failure patients have some form of SDB (p646).
new: CSA is two to three times more prevalent at age 65–90 vs 39–64; an estimated upwards of 50% of stable heart-failure patients have some form of SDB (p646).

old: CPAP pressure usually 5 to 20 cm H2O; well tolerated above age 80 and in mild-moderate dementia (p649).
new: CPAP pressure usually 5 to 20 cm H2O; observational studies found it well tolerated above age 80 and in mild-moderate dementia (p649).

old: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation trials limited to BMI less than 32 kg/m2; cohort of 62 patients aged 65–80 showed benefit (p650).
new: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation trials limited to highly selected CPAP-intolerant patients with BMI less than 32 kg/m2; cohort of 62 patients aged 65–80 showed benefit (p650).

new: Start iron if ferritin less than 75 mcg/L; consider IV iron if ferritin less than 300 mcg/L with moderate-severe symptoms, although IV iron is usually reserved for iron malabsorption (p652).

new: In one study, a third of older patients had persistent severe insomnia at 4-year follow-up; more than 80% of women over 85 report sleeping difficulties (p658).

old: Drugs: Benzodiazepines ↓ sleep latency ~10 minutes, ↑ total sleep time 30 to 60 minutes; avoid long-acting flurazepam/quazepam; all Beers-listed (p659). Temazepam start 7.5 mg, usual 7.5–30 mg, half-life 8.8 h — caution: psychomotor impairment, increased fall risk; eszopiclone start 1 mg, usual 1–2 mg, half-life 6 h — caution: avoid high-fat meals, unpleasant taste/headache (Table 44-5, p660). Zolpidem/zaleplon — rapid onset, take immediately before bed; Beers-listed (p659). Ramelteon (MT1/MT2 agonist) — few side effects, less amnestic (p660). Suvorexant/lemborexant (DORA) — only suvorexant FDA-approved for insomnia with Alzheimer dementia (trial of 277 patients, mild-moderate AD, sleep time up around half an hour after 2 weeks) (p660). Doxepin low-dose 3–6 mg for insomnia vs 100–300 mg as an antidepressant (p661). Avoid diphenhydramine as primary therapy — long half-life, next-day sedation, rapid tolerance, dry mouth, urinary retention, delirium, decreased cognition (p661).
new: Drugs: Benzodiazepines ↓ sleep latency ~10 minutes, ↑ total sleep time 30 to 60 minutes; avoid long-acting flurazepam/quazepam; all Beers-listed (p659). Temazepam start 7.5 mg, usual 7.5–30 mg, half-life 8.8 h — caution: psychomotor impairment, increased fall risk; eszopiclone start 1 mg, usual 1–2 mg, half-life 6 h — caution: avoid high-fat meals, unpleasant taste/headache (Table 44-5, p660). Zolpidem/zaleplon — rapid onset, take immediately before bed; Beers-listed (p659). Ramelteon (MT1/MT2 agonist) — few side effects; lack of amnestic properties makes it somewhat less effective for subjective improvement in sleep (p660). Suvorexant/lemborexant (DORA) — only suvorexant FDA-approved for insomnia with Alzheimer dementia (trial of 277 patients, mild-moderate AD, sleep time up around half an hour after 2 weeks) (p660). Doxepin low-dose 3–6 mg for insomnia vs 100–300 mg as an antidepressant (p661). Avoid diphenhydramine as primary therapy — long half-life, next-day sedation, rapid tolerance, dry mouth, urinary retention, delirium, decreased cognition (p661).

new: No — among residents on high-density foam mattresses, 2.5% (q2h) vs 0.6% (q3h) vs 3.1% (q4h), not significantly different (p684).

new: Pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises: for example, 3 sets/day of 15 contractions, building hold from 3 to 10 seconds (p709).

new: Botulinum toxin A (cystoscopic): early trial results suggest the effect lasts about 6 months (p715).

new: 30%–50% of institutionalized patients with frequent UI also have fecal incontinence — this coexistence suggests common pathophysiologic mechanisms (p716).

new: What is an example of a pelvic floor (Kegel) exercise regimen?

new: For example, three sets daily of 15 contractions, building hold time from 3 to 10 seconds (p709).

new: Assess rehab potential after acute illness resolves — delirium, hemodynamic instability, occult fracture, acute infection may delay referral to rehabilitation (p821).

new: Flexibility: at least 90 degrees knee flexion for stairs; 120 to 150 degrees shoulder flexion/abduction to reach overhead (p825).

old: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a 600k-patient Medicare cohort) (p830). Heart failure: stable 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).
new: Cardiac rehab: only one-third of eligible patients participate (12% in a 600k-patient Medicare cohort) (p830). CR vs. none: mortality 2.3% vs. 5.3%; benefit sustained at 5 years, 16% vs. 25% (p830). ≥25 sessions → 20% lower 5-yr mortality vs. fewer sessions (p830). Heart failure: stable at least 3 to 4 weeks before starting; CR → 28% lower mortality/hospitalization, 29% lower death rate, peak VO2 +15% to 30%, symptoms/ADLs/well-being +15% to 50%; QoL gains seen as early as 2 months (p830).

old: Stroke: rehab can begin as early as 24 to 48 hours poststroke once the patient is medically stable (p831). Dysphagia silent in up to one-third; aphasia in one-third (p831). new: Stroke: rehab can begin as early as 24 to 48 hours poststroke once the patient is medically stable (p831). Dysphagia can be silent in up to one-third of patients with dysphagia; aphasia in one-third (p831). Bladder incontinence 50% to 70% month 1, back to general-population levels by 6 months (p831). Shoulder pain 34% to 84%; depression 15% to 70% (p831).

old: Post-THA (posterolateral): avoid >90 degrees hip flexion early (p832).
new: Post-THA (posterolateral): may need to avoid more than 90 degrees hip flexion early (p832).

new: End of life: delirium in >80% of patients; if sedation is indicated for severe agitated delirium, lorazepam, starting dose 0.5–1.0 mg PO/IV/SQ is the sedation agent of choice (p890).

old: What agent and dose are recommended for sedation in refractory agitated delirium at the end of life?
new: What agent and starting dose are recommended for sedation in severe agitated delirium at the end of life?

old: Citalopram — initial 5–10 mg, max 20 mg/day; CitAD trial showed benefit for agitation, but QTc prolongation and worsened cognition limit its use (p929).
new: Citalopram — initial 5–10 mg, max 20 mg/day; CitAD trial showed benefit for agitation, but QTc prolongation and worsened cognition may limit its use (p929).

new: A Cochrane review found low-certainty evidence that melatonin doses up to 10 mg may have little or no sleep benefit (p931); one small trial of melatonin 3 mg helped agitation/sundowning (p932); ramelteon showed no sleep benefit (p932).

old: Atypical parkinsonisms (PSP, MSA, CBS) have a combined prevalence of 5% to 10% of PD's (p938).
new: Atypical parkinsonisms (PSP, MSA, CBS) have a prevalence of roughly 5% to 10% of PD's (p938).

old: Amantadine — 100 mg BID for PD symptoms, 300–400 mg/day for antidyskinetic effect; confusion, hallucinations, livedo reticularis; poorly tolerated in older adults (p944). Only established effective antidyskinetic agent (antiglutamatergic).
new: Amantadine — usually 100 mg BID for PD symptoms, usually 300–400 mg/day for antidyskinetic effect; confusion, hallucinations, livedo reticularis; often poorly tolerated in older adults (p944). Only established effective antidyskinetic agent (antiglutamatergic).

old: McKeith criteria: probable DLB = 2 core features, or 1 core + 1 suggestive feature (p984).Current practice (not the book): probable DLB = ≥2 core features, or 1 core feature + ≥1 indicative biomarker (reduced DAT uptake on SPECT/PET, abnormal MIBG scintigraphy, or PSG-confirmed REM sleep without atonia) — DLB Consortium 4th consensus report (McKeith et al.), 2017.
new: McKeith criteria: probable DLB = 2 core features, or 1 core + 1 suggestive feature (p984); exam trap: the text says one core plus one supportive feature and classifies RBD as core, while the Table 63-3 footnote says one core plus at least one suggestive feature and the table classifies RBD as suggestive (p984).Current practice (not the book): probable DLB = ≥2 core features, or 1 core feature + ≥1 indicative biomarker (reduced DAT uptake on SPECT/PET, abnormal MIBG scintigraphy, or PSG-confirmed REM sleep without atonia) — DLB Consortium 4th consensus report (McKeith et al.), 2017.

old: Mean survival ~10y, disability progressing ~10%/yr (p983).
new: In postmortem-confirmed DLB cases, mean survival ~10y, disability progressing ~10%/yr (p983).

old: Predictors: older age at motor onset, bradykinesia/non-tremor phenotype, bilateral onset, declining levodopa response, depression, hallucinations (p985).
new: Possible predictors: older age at motor onset, bradykinesia/non-tremor phenotype, bilateral onset, declining levodopa response, depression, hallucinations (p985).

old: Orthostatic dx criterion: ≥30 mmHg systolic BP drop (practically, ≥20 systolic/≥10 diastolic considered significant in the absence of an appropriate heart-rate increase) (p986).
new: Orthostatic dx criterion: ≥30 mmHg systolic BP drop (practically, ≥20 systolic or ≥10 diastolic considered significant in the absence of an appropriate heart-rate increase) (p986).

old: bvFTD accounts for >50% of FTD cases; pathology ~50% tau, ~50% TDP-43, <10% FUS (p987).
new: In most centers, bvFTD accounts for >50% of FTD cases; pathology ~50% tau, ~50% TDP-43, <10% FUS (p987).

old: PPA = isolated language deficit ≥2 years before other decline (p987). nfvPPA: apraxic/agrammatic speech, preserved single-word comprehension; left-dominant atrophy (inferior frontal/insula/caudate); ~20% TDP-43 (type A) at autopsy, remainder tau (CBD > PSP > Pick) (p988). svPPA: fluent but semantically empty speech, surface dyslexia; begins in amygdala/anterior temporal lobe; most behaviorally prominent PPA; usually TDP-43 type C, tau-negative (p988). Logopenic PPA = usually an AD language presentation; may respond to cholinesterase inhibitors (p987).
new: PPA = isolated language deficit ≥2 years before other decline (p987). nfvPPA: apraxic/agrammatic speech, preserved single-word comprehension; left-dominant atrophy (inferior frontal/insula/caudate); ~20% TDP pathology (usually TDP-43 type A) at autopsy, most show tau (CBD > PSP > Pick) (p988). svPPA: fluent but semantically empty speech, surface dyslexia; begins in amygdala/anterior temporal lobe; most behaviorally prominent PPA; often TDP-43 type C-positive, tau-negative inclusions at autopsy (p988). Logopenic PPA = usually an AD language presentation; may respond to cholinesterase inhibitors if imaging or other biomarkers confirm AD etiology (p987-988).

old: Treatment: symptomatic only — SSRIs for behavioral symptoms/cravings/compulsions; atypical neuroleptics only if delusions are problematic; no role for cholinesterase inhibitors (may worsen agitation) (p991).
new: Treatment: symptomatic only — SSRIs for behavioral symptoms/cravings/compulsions; atypical neuroleptics can be considered if delusions are problematic; no theoretical basis for cholinesterase inhibitors (may worsen agitation) (p991).

old: Incidence 1–2/100,000/yr; ~5,000 new US cases/yr; ~2:1 M:F (p991).
new: Incidence 1–2/100,000/yr; ~5,000 new cases/yr; ~2:1 M:F (p991).

old: Symptomatic treatment only; levodopa helps a minority; no role for cholinesterase inhibitors (p992).
new: Symptomatic treatment only; levodopa helps a minority; no theoretical basis for cholinesterase inhibitors (p992).

old: Falls as the first symptom in 60%; downward vertical gaze palsy is more specific than upward (mild vertical gaze limitation is normal with aging), with preserved oculocephalic reflex (p992).
new: Falls as the first symptom in 60%; downward vertical gaze palsy is more specific than upward (mild vertical gaze limitation is normal with aging), with oculocephalic reflex preserved early in disease (p992).

old: Cholinesterase inhibitors — first-line for DLB (often better response than AD, esp. hallucinations); no role in bvFTD/CBD, may worsen agitation (p984, p991–992).
new: Cholinesterase inhibitors — first-line for DLB (often better response than AD, esp. hallucinations); no theoretical basis for use in bvFTD/CBD, may worsen agitation (p984, p991–992).

old: Levodopa — helps parkinsonism in DLB (only after hallucinations/fluctuation are controlled), ~1/3 of MSA patients, and some PSP/CBD patients, but efficacy is limited/wanes (p984, p986, p992).
new: Levodopa — can be used if indicated for parkinsonism in DLB (once hallucinations/fluctuation are controlled), ~1/3 of MSA patients, and some PSP/CBD patients, but efficacy is limited/wanes (p984, p986, p992).

old: המשמעות הקלינית: האוטונומיה של חולה כשיר גוברת — אך לפני שמכבדים סירוב, יש חובה לנסות לשכנע אותו לקבל לפחות חמצן, מזון ונוזלים, טיפולים שגרתיים למחלות בו-זמניות/רקע, וטיפול מקל (פליאטיבי).
new: המשמעות הקלינית: יש לכבד את רצונו של חולה הנוטה למות בעל כשרות שאינו רוצה שחייו יוארכו ולהימנע מטיפול בו (§15(א)).

old: אם לאחר מאמץ סביר הוא עדיין מסרב — מכבדים את הסירוב, כולל למזון ונוזלים.
new: בנפרד, על המטפלים לעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנעו לקבל חמצן, מזון ונוזלים אף באמצעים מלאכותיים, טיפולים שגרתיים למחלות בו-זמניות או למחלות רקע וטיפול מקל (§15(ב)).

old: הערה (פרשנות, לא לשון החוק): אין ניגוד בין הוראות אלה; זהו מדרג מכוון: כשיר (15) — סירובו מכובד, גם למזון/נוזלים, לאחר מאמץ סביר לשכנע; לא כשיר, לא בשלב סופי (16) — טיפול נלווה (כולל מזון ונוזלים) מוגן תמיד; לא כשיר, בשלב סופי (17) — נמנעים גם מטיפול נלווה, אך נוזלים מוגנים אלא אם גורמים סבל/נזק.
new: הערה (פרשנות, לא לשון החוק): אין ניגוד בין הוראות אלה; זהו מדרג מכוון: כשיר (15) — סירובו מכובד, גם למזון/נוזלים, ולצד זאת מוטלת חובה נפרדת לעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע; לא כשיר, לא בשלב סופי (16) — טיפול נלווה (כולל מזון ונוזלים) מוגן תמיד; לא כשיר, בשלב סופי (17) — נמנעים גם מטיפול נלווה, אך נוזלים מוגנים אלא אם גורמים סבל/נזק.

old: אם נמנע מהמטופל לחתום — הסכמה בפני שני עדים (§14(ג)); במצב חירום רפואי — בעל פה, ותיעוד בכתב סמוך ככל האפשר (§14(ד)).
new: אם נמנע מהמטופל לחתום — הסכמה בפני שני עדים, ובלבד שדבר ההסכמה והעדות יתועדו בכתב סמוך ככל האפשר לאחר מכן (§14(ג)); במצב חירום רפואי — בעל פה, ותיעוד בכתב סמוך ככל האפשר (§14(ד)).

old: (נוהל 3.4.2 עוסק במטופלים שכבר ב"קוד" משרד הבריאות; לקבלה חדשה לאשפוז מסובסד, ה"סיווג" כסיעודי או תשוש נפש נעשה ע"י הגריאטר המחוזי באמצעות ועדה לפי נוהל 01-09 שבחוזר מינהל רפואה 20/2009, סעיף 3.3 — אותה שרשרת; נוהל 01-09 אינו עוסק בסיעודי-מורכב או בשיקום.)
new: (נוהל 3.4.2 מסדיר קבלה של מטופל חדש שלא היה במימון "קוד" קודם לכן (§3.2), וכן שינוי סטטוס למימון משרד הבריאות המחייב קבלה מלאה וטופס הפניה רשמי גם בהעברה בתוך המוסד (§5.2); לקבלה חדשה לאשפוז מסובסד, ה"סיווג" כסיעודי או תשוש נפש נעשה ע"י הגריאטר המחוזי באמצעות ועדה לפי נוהל 01-09 שבחוזר מינהל רפואה 20/2009, סעיף 3.3 — אותה שרשרת; נוהל 01-09 אינו עוסק בסיעודי-מורכב או בשיקום.)

old: לעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע אותו לקבל מזון ונוזלים (אף באמצעים מלאכותיים), חמצן, טיפולים שגרתיים למחלות בו-זמניות/רקע וטיפול מקל — ורק אז, אם הוא עדיין מסרב, לכבד את סירובו (§15).
new: לכבד את רצונו ולהימנע מטיפול רפואי בו (§15(א)); בנפרד, לעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנעו לקבל חמצן, מזון ונוזלים (אף באמצעים מלאכותיים), טיפולים שגרתיים למחלות בו-זמניות/רקע וטיפול מקל (§15(ב)).

old: Medications: withdrawing centrally-acting drugs did NOT significantly reduce falls in the most recent systematic review (5 trials, 1309 participants; RaR 0.98, 95% CI 0.63–1.51) — better to prevent uptake than deprescribe later (p639). Avoid prescribing benzodiazepines/z-drugs/other psychotropics for insomnia unless there is a clear pattern of addiction or inability to complete a withdrawal program; consider nonpharmacological approaches (p639). Vitamin D: no benefit in community-dwelling older adults (even if deficient); may reduce falls in RACF residents (p639).
new: Medications: withdrawing centrally-acting drugs did NOT significantly reduce falls in the most recent systematic review (5 trials, 1309 participants; RaR 0.98, 95% CI 0.63–1.51) — better to prevent uptake than deprescribe later (p639). Avoid prescribing benzodiazepines/z-drugs/other psychotropics for insomnia unless there is a clear pattern of addiction or inability to complete a withdrawal program; consider nonpharmacological approaches (p639). old: Drugs (Table 44-2, p653): Ropinirole 0.25–4 mg, Pramipexole 0.125–2 mg — caution: augmentation, behavioral disinhibition. Gabapentin enacarbil 600–1200 mg (only α2δ ligand FDA-approved for RLS), gabapentin 100–1800 mg, pregabalin 300 mg — caution: sedation, suicidal ideation. Clonazepam 0.25–2 mg, temazepam 15–30 mg — limited evidence, cognitive risk. old: Oxybutynin (antimuscarinic) 2.5–5 mg tid — dry mouth, blurry vision, ↑ intraocular pressure, delirium, constipation (p712); patients with dementia must be followed for drug-induced delirium (p713).
new: Oxybutynin (antimuscarinic) 2.5–5 mg tid — dry mouth, blurry vision, ↑ intraocular pressure, delirium, constipation (p712); patients with dementia must be followed for drug-induced delirium (p713); Current practice (not the book): offer an antimuscarinic or beta-3 agonist for OAB (Strong recommendation, Grade A); counsel on side effects and potential dementia/cognitive risk with antimuscarinics (Clinical Principles), using shared decision-making and patient preferences; when pharmacotherapy is indicated, consider a beta-3 agonist trial first, as typically preferred in the guideline discussion - AUA/SUFU 2024, statements 16-18 and discussion, p24-27

old: Vaginal estrogen ring — 1 ring every 3 months, for atrophic-vaginitis-related urgency UI; contraindicated with gynecologic cancer history, relative contraindication with breast cancer history (Table 47-12, p712).
new: Vaginal estrogen ring — 1 ring every 3 months, for atrophic-vaginitis-related urgency UI; contraindicated with gynecologic cancer history, relative contraindication with breast cancer history (Table 47-12, p712); Required reading: see AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for systemic versus low-dose vaginal estrogen and the breast-cancer discussion qualification (Table 2, p2061)

old: Screening tools (Table 58-3, p884): 4AT scores 0–12, ≥4 suggests delirium; Nu-DESC scores 0–10.
new: Screening tools (Table 58-3, p884): 4AT scores 0–12, ≥4 suggests delirium; Nu-DESC scores 0–10; Current practice (not the book): when delirium indicators are present, a competent practitioner should assess with 4AT; use CAM-ICU or ICDSC in critical care or the recovery room after surgery; a healthcare professional with relevant expertise makes the final diagnosis if assessment indicates delirium - NICE CG103, recommendations updated 2023, 1.6.1-1.6.2, p11

old: Beers-listed culprits (Table 58-2, p883): anticholinergics, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, corticosteroids, H2-blockers, meperidine, Z-drugs (zolpidem/eszopiclone/zaleplon), TCAs. Psychoactive drugs should be discontinued or minimized whenever possible (p885).
new: Beers-listed culprits (Table 58-2, p883): anticholinergics, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, corticosteroids, H2-blockers, meperidine, Z-drugs (zolpidem/eszopiclone/zaleplon), TCAs. Psychoactive drugs should be discontinued or minimized whenever possible (p885); Required reading: see AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for opioids and delirium, including the balanced pain-management caveat (Table 3, p2066)

old: Pimavanserin 34 mg/day — FDA-approved for Parkinson disease psychosis; confusion, edema, hypotension (p928).
new: Pimavanserin 34 mg/day — FDA-approved for Parkinson disease psychosis; confusion, edema, hypotension (p928); Current practice (not the book): brexpiprazole received FDA approval in May 2023 for agitation associated with Alzheimer dementia; its boxed warning states increased mortality in older patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotics - AGS Alternatives 2025, Table 3 footnote e, p12; FDA announcement, 11 May 2023, approval and boxed-warning paragraphs

old: DBS (STN or GPi target) — FDA-approved 2002; for motor fluctuations/dyskinesias or medication-refractory tremor; does not improve postural instability or other axial features (p949).
new: DBS (STN or GPi target) — FDA-approved 2002; for motor fluctuations/dyskinesias or medication-refractory tremor; does not improve postural instability or other axial features (p949); Current practice (not the book): NICE recommends subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion as an option for adults with advanced levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease, severe motor fluctuations and hyperkinesia or dyskinesia despite available medicines, only when apomorphine or DBS cannot be used or no longer controls symptoms and the commercial arrangement applies; FDA approved it on 16 October 2024 for motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson disease - NICE TA934 2023, 1.1 p4; FDA NDA216962 approval package cover and approval letter p1

old: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health.
new: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health; Current practice (not the book): individualize targets (grade C): healthy older adults with few stable illnesses and intact cognition/function should have lower goals such as A1C <7.0-7.5% and/or CGM time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥70% and time ≤70 mg/dL ≤4%; complex/intermediate health prioritizes hypoglycemia avoidance, with less stringent goals such as A1C <8.0%, time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥50% and time <70 mg/dL <1%, considering cognition/function, frailty, comorbidity, medication risk-benefit and preferences; very complex/poor health avoids reliance on A1C and focuses on avoiding hypoglycemia and symptomatic hyperglycemia, with no numerical CGM goal specified; fasting/premeal and bedtime ranges respectively are 80-130/80-180 mg/dL (healthy), 90-150/100-180 (complex/intermediate) and 100-180/110-200 (very complex/poor); lower A1C goals require no recurrent/severe hypoglycemia or undue treatment burden - ADA Standards of Care 2026, Section 13, recommendations 13.7a-c pS282 and Table 13.2 pS284

old: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579).
new: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579); Required reading: see AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for qualified sulfonylurea avoidance and the preference if one is used (Table 2, p2061)

old: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; one prospective cohort study associated cataract surgery with fewer falls provided post-op spectacle lens power updates were cautious (less than ±0.75 diopter change) (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).
new: Vision: first-eye cataract surgery → 34% fewer falls; second-eye surgery similar (~32%) but not statistically significant; one prospective cohort study associated cataract surgery with fewer falls provided post-op spectacle lens power updates were cautious (less than ±0.75 diopter change) (p639). Updating glasses to correct prescription: evidence less clear — one RCT found no significant reduction, and another (vision assessment + treatment) increased falls by ~50% (p639). Single-lens distance glasses plus counseling about ground-level hazards for habitual multifocal wearers: 40% fewer falls in the outdoor-active subgroup (p639). Home-safety modification for severe uncorrectable low vision: 41% fewer falls (p639).

old: Movement is the key screen: none developed PI with >50 spontaneous body movements/night vs 90% PI with ≤20 movements/night (p682).
new: In one monitored geriatric study, none developed PI with >50 spontaneous body movements/night vs 90% PI with ≤20 movements/night (p682).

old: Ultrasound detects damage before clinical signs: ~80% with abnormal images had no documented erythema (p686).
new: Early work suggests ultrasound may detect damage before clinical signs: ~80% with abnormal images had no documented erythema (p686).

old: PVR interpretation: PVR < 100 mL normal; PVR > 200 mL abnormal; 100–200 mL is equivocal (p707).
new: PVR interpretation: PVR < 100 mL without straining generally reflects adequate emptying; PVR > 200 mL abnormal; 100–200 mL is equivocal (p707).

old: Diabetic foot disease: Medicare covers one pair of shoes/inserts each year (p829).
new: Diabetes and severe diabetic foot disease: Medicare covers one pair of therapeutic shoes and inserts or shoe modifications each year (p829).

old: NIA-AA dementia criteria (Table 59-1): decline from previous level that interferes with function, not explained by delirium or major psychiatric disorder; history from patient and a knowledgeable informant + objective cognitive assessment (p895).
new: NIA-AA dementia criteria (Table 59-1): decline from previous level that interferes with function, not explained by delirium or major psychiatric disorder; history from patient and a knowledgeable informant + objective cognitive assessment; impairment involves at least two cognitive or behavioral domains (p895).

old: AChEIs (mainstay): donepezil (Aricept), galantamine (Razadyne), rivastigmine (Exelon) — the text says start low with dose increases approximately every 2 months (p911), while Table 59-7 lists drug-specific steps: donepezil 4–6 wk before 5→10 mg (the 10→23 mg step after 3 months on 10 mg) (p912), galantamine ≥4 wk per step (p912), rivastigmine ≥2 wk per oral step or 4–6 wk for the patch (p913); 18–48% show cognitive improvement, most others just have slowed decline (p911). Cautions: GI upset (take with food); bradycardia/AV block/syncope/weight loss are triggers to deprescribe.
new: AChEIs (mainstay): donepezil (Aricept), galantamine (Razadyne), rivastigmine (Exelon) — the text says start low with dose increases approximately every 2 months (p911), while Table 59-7 lists drug-specific steps: donepezil 4–6 wk before 5→10 mg (the 10→23 mg step after 3 months on 10 mg) (p912), galantamine ≥4 wk per step (p912), rivastigmine ≥2 wk per oral step or 4–6 wk for the patch (p912); 18–48% show cognitive improvement, most others just have slowed decline (p911). Cautions: GI upset (take with food); bradycardia/AV block/syncope/weight loss are triggers to deprescribe.

old: Memantine (Namenda) — NMDA-receptor antagonist, approved for moderate-to-severe AD; combo with an AChEI is not superior to either drug alone (p911).
new: Memantine (Namenda) — NMDA-receptor antagonist, approved for moderate-to-severe AD; combo with an AChEI has not been shown to be superior to either drug alone (p911).

old: Feeding tubes are not recommended in advanced AD — they do not prolong survival or improve comfort, and do not reduce pressure sores, infection, or aspiration risk (p916).
new: Feeding tubes are not recommended in advanced AD — they do not prolong survival or improve comfort, and have not been shown to reduce pressure sores, infection, or aspiration risk (p916).

old: New-onset acute NPS work-up: CBC, chem panel, LFTs, UA/culture; consider TSH, B12, folate, tox screen, ECG; chest x-ray if respiratory signs; imaging particularly if focal signs; EEG if seizure suspected; CSF rarely needed — only if meningitis/encephalitis suspected (p922).
new: New-onset acute NPS work-up: CBC, chem panel, LFTs, UA/culture; consider TSH, B12, folate, tox screen, ECG; chest x-ray if respiratory signs; imaging particularly if focal signs; EEG if seizure suspected; CSF rarely needed — indicated if meningitis/encephalitis suspected (p922).

old: Delirium-related agitation (short-term, low-dose), all q6h PRN: haloperidol 0.25–0.5 mg PO/IV, quetiapine 12.5–25 mg PO, olanzapine 2.5 mg PO or 1.25–2.5 mg IM, or risperidone 0.25–0.5 mg PO/IV (p923).Current practice (not the book): risperidone is not given IV; the only injectable form (Risperdal Consta) is IM only — "Do not administer intravenously" — Risperdal Consta prescribing information (Janssen).
new: Delirium-related agitation (short-term, low-dose), all q6h PRN: haloperidol 0.25–0.5 mg PO/IV, quetiapine 12.5–25 mg PO, olanzapine 2.5 mg PO or 1.25–2.5 mg IM, or risperidone 0.25–0.5 mg PO/IV (p923).Current practice (not the book): risperidone is not given IV; Risperdal Consta is IM only — "Do not administer intravenously" — Risperdal Consta prescribing information (Janssen).

old: Peak-dose dyskinesia: reduce levodopa dose, or add amantadine (start 100 mg BID, up to 200 mg BID); buspirone up to 20 mg/day (p946).
new: Peak-dose dyskinesia: reduce levodopa dose, or add amantadine (start 100 mg BID, up to 200 mg BID); buspirone up to 20 mg/day may benefit some patients (p946).

old: Possible bvFTD needs 3 of 6 core symptoms (early disinhibition, apathy, loss of sympathy/empathy, repetitive motor behaviors, hyperorality, executive deficit) (p982).
new: Possible bvFTD needs 3 of 6 core symptoms (early disinhibition, apathy, loss of sympathy/empathy, repetitive motor behaviors, hyperorality, frontal executive deficit with relative visuospatial sparing) (p982).

old: Osteoarthritis (OA): 60% of adults ≥65 yr have arthritis/chronic joint pain (p1066); intra-articular steroid (40–80 mg depot preparation, verified against the page image) is more effective than placebo in the short term (<3 months), long-term benefit not well established; hyaluronic acid typically 1–5 injections; platelet-rich plasma (PRP) shows efficacy up to 12 months in some studies (p1067)
new: Osteoarthritis (OA): 60% of adults ≥65 yr have arthritis/chronic joint pain (p1066); for knee OA, intra-articular steroid (40–80 mg depot preparation, verified against the page image) is more effective than placebo in the short term (<3 months), long-term benefit not well established; hyaluronic acid typically 1–5 injections; platelet-rich plasma (PRP) shows promising efficacy in knee OA up to 12 months in some studies; hip HA/PRP efficacy needs further study (p1067)

old: Table 75-6 tiers — indications (actual replacement criteria): symptomatic + severe AI regardless of LV function, OR asymptomatic + severe AI + EF < 50%, OR severe AI undergoing other cardiac surgery; considerations: asymptomatic, normal LV function, dilated ventricle with LVESD > 50 mm, or moderate AI undergoing other cardiac surgery; possible indication: asymptomatic, normal function, progressive LV dilatation > 65 mm if surgical risk is low (table does not name the dimension; the text calls it LVESD) (p1155).Current practice (not the book): the 65-mm AR threshold is LV end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD >65 mm, progressive, low surgical risk: may be considered); LVESD >50 mm is the end-systolic trigger — ACC/AHA valvular guideline, 2020.
new: Table 75-6 tiers — indications (actual replacement criteria): symptomatic + severe AI regardless of LV function, OR asymptomatic + severe AI + EF < 50%, OR severe AI undergoing other cardiac surgery; considerations: asymptomatic, severe AI, normal LV function, dilated ventricle with LVESD > 50 mm, or moderate AI undergoing other cardiac surgery; possible indication: asymptomatic, severe AI, normal function, progressive LV dilatation > 65 mm if surgical risk is low (table does not name the dimension; the text calls it LVESD) (p1155).Current practice (not the book): the 65-mm AR threshold is LV end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD >65 mm, progressive, low surgical risk: may be considered); LVESD >50 mm is the end-systolic trigger — ACC/AHA valvular guideline, 2020.

old: Repair durability: reoperation rate ~7–10% at 10 yr, said to equal replacement's own reoperation rate (p1159).
new: Repair durability, as printed: freedom from reoperation equaling that of valve replacement (7%–10% at 10 years) (p1159).

old: Spironolactone — 12.5–50 mg daily; eplerenone — 25–50 mg daily; both contraindicated if creatinine ≥2.5 mg/dL or hyperkalemia (p1181).Current practice (not the book): eGFR ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m² or serum potassium ≥5.0 mEq/L are contraindications to MRA initiation — AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline, 2022.
new: Spironolactone — 12.5–50 mg daily; eplerenone — 25–50 mg daily; both contraindicated if creatinine ≥2.5 mg/dL or hyperkalemia; SGLT2 inhibitors reduced death and HF hospitalizations in HFREF in DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced, with similar efficacy over age 75 and regardless of diabetes (p1181).Current practice (not the book): eGFR ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m² or serum potassium ≥5.0 mEq/L are contraindications to MRA initiation — AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline, 2022.

old: Azithromycin 250 mg daily or 3×/week reduces exacerbations in former smokers; watch for QTc, hearing loss, resistance (p1254).
new: Azithromycin 250 mg daily or 3×/week reduces exacerbations in former smokers; watch for QTc, hearing loss, resistance; maintenance may be considered for frequent exacerbators despite maximal triple inhalers when worsening airflow obstruction and airway inflammation drive symptoms, without hearing impairment, resting tachycardia or other arrhythmia, apparent QTc-prolongation risk, or clinical/radiographic NTM evidence, with NTM assessment before regular use (p1254).

old: Renal vein renin ratio ≥1.5 between kidneys predicts a beneficial BP response to revascularization; failure to lateralize does not predict a negative response (p1289).
new: Renal vein renin ratio ≥1.5 between kidneys predicts a beneficial BP response to revascularization; failure to lateralize does not predict a negative response; overall BP response cannot be predicted confidently with renal vein renin measurements (p1289).

old: Rome IV: ≥2 of the following, on >25% of occasions, for ≥12 wk in the last 12 mo: ≤2 BM/week, straining, hard stool (Bristol 1-2), sensation of incomplete evacuation, sensation of anorectal obstruction, manual maneuvers to defecate (p1354).
new: Rome IV: ≥2 of the following, on >25% of occasions, for ≥12 wk in the last 12 mo: ≤2 BM/week, straining, hard stool (Bristol 1-2), sensation of incomplete evacuation, sensation of anorectal obstruction, manual maneuvers to defecate; loose stools rarely occur without laxatives and IBS criteria are not fulfilled (p1354).

old: Normal perineal descent is <4 cm (p1365). Plain x-ray: megacolon = colon diameter >6.5 cm; rectal dilatation >4 cm implies dysmotility (p1365).
new: Normal perineal descent is <4 cm (p1365). Plain x-ray: colon diameter >6.5 cm without acute obstruction points toward megacolon; rectal dilatation >4 cm implies dysmotility (p1365).
